title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: Exclusive: Meta and Amazon discuss ending Muse shopping bot blockade, as ads, search emerge as key issues
items.content_text: Meta Platforms and Amazon are negotiating the potential integration of Meta's Muse AI agent into Amazon's e-commerce platform, seeking to reverse a block imposed two months ago. The core tensions involve potential cannibalization of Amazon's advertising revenue and the risks of disintermediation between brands and their end consumers.

items.title: Australia passes the Digital Duty of Care Act, an online safety law that exposes Big Tech to multibillion-dollar fines for failing to prevent foreseeable harms (Rod McGuirk/Associated Press)
items.content_text: The Australian Parliament has passed the Digital Duty of Care Act, legally mandating that Big Tech companies take proactive measures to prevent foreseeable online harms. Backed by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's government, the legislation allows for fines of up to 5% of global revenue, though it faces intense criticism over potential political censorship and free speech concerns.

items.title: AI is straining America’s open records systems
items.content_text: AI-powered automation is triggering a surge in public records requests across the U.S., forcing local agencies to handle significantly increased volume and scope. This influx has strained the limited resources of town and state offices, leading some jurisdictions to consider legislative changes to limit transparency requirements, potentially hindering open government.

items.title: Flipkart CEO to Exit After Transforming Walmart’s India Play
items.content_text: Walmart’s president and CEO Doug McMillon (left) with Flipkart co-founder Binny Bansal. items.title: Chinese EDA software provider Phlexing says it has been collaborating with Huawei since 2019 to develop a suite of EDA tools based on Huawei's Tau Scaling Law (Nikkei Asia)
items.content_text: Huawei and Phlexing Technology have collaborated since 2019 to integrate chip architecture, workflows, and EDA tools. Leveraging Huawei’s 'Tau Scaling Law,' the project aims to resolve automation challenges in advanced chip design, circumventing US-imposed Entity List restrictions.

items.title: Brussels presses porn sites to introduce tougher age checks
items.content_text: The European Commission is pressuring adult platforms, including Pornhub, Stripchat, XNXX, and XVideos, to implement more robust age verification. This effort aligns with the development of a bloc-wide age verification application aimed at enhancing minor protection in the digital space.

items.title: Huawei says HarmonyOS has surpassed 100M installations across smartphones, tablets, and PCs, offering 460K+ apps and services from 12M+ registered developers (Iris Deng/South China Morning Post)
items.content_text: Huawei Technologies announced that HarmonyOS has surpassed 100 million installations across smartphones, tablets, and PCs, supported by over 460,000 apps and 12 million registered developers. Richard Yu Chengdong, Chairman of the Consumer Business Group, stated that the ecosystem has crossed a critical scale threshold, signaling the system's transition to a mature, self-reliant software platform independent of Google’s mobile services.

items.title: Sources: Samsung and SK Hynix agree to adopt parts of YMTC's "Xtacking" tech for 3D NAND flash via cross-licensing deals, signaling YMTC's rapid tech progress (Nikkei Asia)
items.content_text: Global memory leaders Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix have integrated Yangtze Memory Technologies Co.'s (YMTC) Xtacking architecture via cross-licensing deals, utilizing independent CMOS and cell wafer bonding to optimize 3D NAND performance. This adoption confirms YMTC’s rapid technical maturation and patent portfolio depth, marking a significant milestone in China's semiconductor industrial self-sufficiency.

items.title: Amazon Targets UK Car Buyers Being Reeled In by Chinese Brands
items.content_text: Amazon.com Inc. has announced plans to launch online car retail services in the UK by early 2027. This expansion builds upon its established US footprint, where it currently facilitates new and used car sales across 35 brands in over 150 cities, signaling a push to capture automotive market share through e-commerce channels.

items.title: ‘Tech bros strike back’ as Donald Trump rescues Nvidia’s Jensen Huang
items.content_text: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been reinstated after Silicon Valley investors, including Marc Andreessen, lobbied Vice President JD Vance and President Trump. Despite national security concerns raised by Secretary of State Marco Rubio regarding alleged spy ties, Trump prioritized the AI-led economic boom and tech market stability, supported by Attorney General Todd Blanche’s confirmation of no evidence of wrongdoing.

items.title: NJ-based AidenAI, which helps enterprises integrate AI into apps, data infrastructure, and business workflows, raised a $32M Series A led by A91 Partners (Anne Florentyna/Inc42)
items.content_text: Enterprise AI startup AidenAI has raised $32 Mn (₹297.1 Cr) in a Series A funding round led by growth investment firm A91 Partners, as it looks to expand its AI platform and engineering capabilities. The fresh capital will be used to invest in its platform and engineering talent as it looks to scale its global enterprise AI business. “With A91 as our partner, we are excited to invest in our people and platforms and help shape the next wave of enterprise technology services,” AidenAI founder and

items.title: EU plans €50bn tech fund to close gap with US and China
items.content_text: The EU is drawing up plans to mobilise up to €50bn for a new fund that would make long-term, high-risk investments in European artificial intelligence and quantum computing companies, as Brussels seeks to reduce its dependence on US and Chinese technology. The proposed Sovereign Tech Equity Fund (Stef) would make larger, riskier and longer-term investments than existing EU financing schemes, according to two officials involved in the discussions. “These are long-term, stable investments in ris

items.title: How Meta is using Instagram to get an ad boost from its Muse personal AI agent
items.content_text: Meta is integrating Instagram's user saving habits into its Muse personal AI agent to drive ad conversions. With 25% of Muse users engaged in shopping at an average transaction value exceeding $200, Meta has captured a 51% market share in agentic shopping, significantly outpacing Grok and ChatGPT.

items.title: Officials Brief Congressional Staff on Intelligence Surrounding Nvidia Affair
items.content_text: Officials from the FBI, CIA, and ODNI briefed congressional intelligence committees on Alice Huang, who operated the Singapore-based Megaspeed firm suspected of diverting Nvidia AI chips to China. Intelligence indicates her ties to the Chinese Ministry of State Security, with her husband, Kang Wei, identified as a more significant intelligence asset. While high-level statements downplay criminal charges, Congress is demanding the release of the classified memo from Secretary of State Marco Rubio regarding these relationships.

items.title: Rajiv Ramaswami to step down as Nutanix begins hunt for its next CEO
items.content_text: Nutanix CEO Rajiv Ramaswami has announced his departure, triggering a leadership search and a transition period where he will serve as a senior advisor. Despite beating Q1 expectations with a 15% revenue increase, the company's conservative full-year guidance triggered an 8% drop in after-hours stock trading.

items.title: HP Gives Profit Forecast Signaling Better Handle on Memory Costs
items.content_text: HP Inc. issued a fiscal profit forecast exceeding analyst consensus. The company aims to stabilize margins in a challenging PC and printer market by demonstrating improved control over volatile memory supply chain costs and structural efficiency.

items.title: A history professor says GPT-6.2 Astra solved a historical mystery in 22 minutes by identifying the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale (Mark Humphries/Generative History)
items.content_text: A history professor utilized GPT-6.2 Astra to identify the author of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale University within 22 minutes. The model successfully performed complex contextual reconstruction and archival cross-referencing, demonstrating a breakthrough in processing unstructured historical datasets.

items.title: US financial crimes bureau discloses ‘cybersecurity incident’
items.content_text: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) of the U.S. Treasury has confirmed unauthorized access to a subset of its systems and initiated an investigation. FinCEN, responsible for anti-money laundering, has taken systems offline as a precaution while maintaining reporting channels via hotline.

items.title: SoftBank drops over 11% as Wall Street AI sell-off ripples across Asian tech names
items.content_text: Asian semiconductor stocks faced a rout following skepticism over ROI on AI capital expenditures and volatility in U.S. markets. Major suppliers including Tokyo Electron, Advantest, Samsung Electronics, and SK Hynix saw significant share price declines as AI accelerator demand confidence wavered.

items.title: Workday shares fall as soft subscription forecast overshadows third-quarter beat
items.content_text: Workday reported third-quarter adjusted EPS of $2.82 and revenue of $2.705 billion, both exceeding analyst targets. However, the stock fell over 7% due to a conservative subscription revenue outlook. CEO Aneel Bhusri emphasized AI product growth and the acquisition of ConductorOne to strengthen agentic automation.

items.title: Utah prosecutors drop criminal charges against Kalshi and its co-founders, one day after the company halted operations in the state (Marshall Cohen/CNN)
items.content_text: Utah Attorney General Derek Brown dropped criminal charges against prediction market Kalshi and its founders after the company ceased operations in the state. This move signals an ongoing struggle between state anti-gambling laws and federal financial market regulation, with civil litigation still pending.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Return Shows Nvidia Is Too Big to Police
items.content_text: Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang just 11 days after his resignation, citing assurances from high-level U.S. government officials. However, intelligence experts warn that this move risks undermining national security enforcement, particularly as the company faces a criminal probe regarding alleged chip diversion to China.

items.title: WiseTech’s White Cleared in Human Trafficking Probe by Police
items.content_text: Australian police have concluded their investigation into Richard White, founder of WiseTech Global Ltd., following allegations of exploitation involving immigration status. The authorities decided to take no further action, effectively clearing the executive of the reported criminal allegations.

items.title: Trump leaves door open to Jensen Huang pardon — and urges him not to plead 5th to Congress next week
items.content_text: President Trump has publicly backed Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO, advising him to speak truthfully in upcoming congressional hearings rather than invoking the Fifth Amendment. Trump suggested that a presidential pardon remains an option, aiming to stabilize the firm amid intense congressional scrutiny over export controls and national security.

items.title: ‘The king is back!’ Huang’s return to Nvidia is greeted with relief in Asia.
items.content_text: The reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO triggered a strong rally in Asian markets, particularly in Taiwan, Japan, and South Korea. Despite prior controversy surrounding his personal life and geopolitical ties, the regional tech ecosystem views his return as a critical signal for the continued stability of the global AI supply chain.

items.title: Turn artifacts into Mac and Windows apps
items.content_text: Anthropic has launched the 'Install as app' beta for Claude on Mac and Windows, enabling users to transform Artifacts into standalone desktop applications with dedicated windows and system tray notifications. These apps can leverage Claude’s capabilities and local connectors under granular permission controls, facilitating deeper integration into professional workflows.

items.title: Dell lifts annual forecasts after record quarter on surging AI server demand
items.content_text: Dell Technologies has raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts for the third time this year, fueled by record demand for AI infrastructure, with fiscal 2027 revenue now projected at $202 billion. Despite slower growth in the PC segment, Dell reported a record $132.3 billion backlog in AI servers, underscoring an accelerating refresh cycle for data center hardware.

items.title: Docs: Grubhub is on track for ~$6.4B in GTV and a $97M EBITDA loss in 2026, reflecting heavy marketing and operating costs; Wonder says it's not pursuing a sale (Valida Pau/The Information)
items.content_text: Marc Lore's Wonder is not pursuing a sale of Grubhub, Wonder says, after preliminary sales talks with Amazon and Walmart.

items.title: OpenAI Staffer Charged With Planting Bug Released on Bond
items.content_text: Former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan was charged by federal prosecutors after installing hidden audio recorders in an executive conference room. OpenAI utilized internal AI tools to assist FBI investigations, confirming that no model weights or source code were compromised, and Alfozan has been released on bond.
